LHX.sentence: L3Harris is basically flat today, but it's trading nearly a third below its high — unusual for a defense contractor when military spending is on a steady upward path, so nothing about the business has really changed.

ASML.sentence: ASML dropped about 8% and is well off its highs, but this is the one company in the world that makes the machines needed to print the most advanced chips, so the demand story hasn't changed — just the price.

LIN.sentence: Linde is having a quiet week — industrial gas demand is steady and they keep nudging prices up a little each quarter under long contracts, which is the whole, pleasantly boring story with this one.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is quiet — their cloud business keeps growing fast as AI demand builds, and the story just keeps grinding along without any drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher is down a bit while the lab-equipment market is near the bottom of a slow patch — their growth is sluggish for now, and a recovery hasn't shown up in the numbers yet.

CVX.sentence: Chevron is flat this week — its profits are swollen by today's unusually high oil prices from the Persian Gulf disruptions, so the thing worth watching is whether that extra cash flows through to shareholders, not the oil price itself.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow has fallen hard — well off its high — even though big companies and government agencies keep signing up for its workflow and AI tools on long contracts, so this is the price dropping, not the business breaking.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore ticked up while pure copper miners sold off, because investors are giving it credit for its huge commodity-trading arm, which steadies things when metal prices fall.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta dropped about 6%, but the price it gets for a ton of crushed stone is still creeping up faster than its costs — the part that actually matters — so the pullback isn't about the business.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA, the big Latin American Coke bottler, is down slightly mostly because the Mexican peso has weakened a little, which trims the value of its earnings when converted to dollars.

UBER.sentence: Uber dipped a touch, but people keep booking a lot more rides and food orders than before — the real thing to watch is whether the self-driving companies choose to put their cars on Uber's app or go it alone.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant, is trading below what its fleet of ships would cost to replace — the kind of rock-bottom pricing you see when a cyclical business is out of favor.

MA.sentence: Mastercard dipped and is unusually trading a touch cheaper than its twin Visa, which almost never happens, but people keep tapping their cards more than ever, so nothing is actually broken here.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical robot company is down a few percent, but hospitals keep doing more operations with its machines, and since most of its money comes from the supplies each surgery uses, the underlying demand keeps compounding.

NVDA.sentence: Nvidia fell about 9% after Amazon and Google's parent showed they're now spending more on computing gear than their businesses bring in and borrowing the rest — nothing changed at Nvidia itself, but those are the customers who pay its bills, so whether they can keep spending is the whole question.
